title: Rings of the right (left) almost stable range $1$: the diagonal reduction theorem for Hermite rings of almost stable range $1$ (Theorem 12)
author: Victor Bovdi and Bohdan Zabavsky
work: Rings of the right (left) almost stable range $1$
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is a research-level statement of noncommutative ring theory - a diagonal reduction for an arbitrary Hermite ring of almost stable range 1 - and its proof is the longest single argument attached to any of the paper's Hermite-ring results. With the paper's own prerequisites supplied as context (the definitions of right and left almost stable range 1, of B\'ezout, Hermite and L-rings, Lemma 1 on the completability consequences of stable range 2, and Theorem 8, which produces the element lambda with (lambda a+b)R+cR=dR), the proof still has to be assembled: it must pass from the hypothesis RaR+RbR+RcR=R to that lambda, carry out the explicit 2x2 transformations through a unimodular row, use the fact that a Hermite ring is a B\'ezout ring of stable range 2 twice, complete the unimodular column to an invertible matrix, and then close with the two-sided ideal computation R=RdR in RzR that gives RzR=R. None of this is examined at the level of an ordinary PhD qualifying examination, where ring theory is examined through modules over Noetherian or principal ideal rings and the standard structure theorems; stable range, Hermite rings, completability of unimodular columns and two-sided ideal arithmetic of this kind belong to research practice. The techniques are however the paper's own standard toolkit, so the unit is recorded as H2 rather than H3.
